thread:
devon: heads-up — CI canary shows a ~2.3x p95 slowdown on decode path after yesterday's merge (commit d4f7b9c). reproduction in our canary runs.

maya: who owns the merged change?

devon: arnav landed the fused-op scheduler tweak + a kernel preference change. He was trying to reduce small-batch overhead.

arnav: that was the scheduler patch (PR #3281). I did add a new heuristic to prefer attentn_v2 on multihead shapes. I saw improvements in bench runs tho. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3281

zach: perf-bot flagged the canary on node group "canary-decode-3" at 03:12 UTC:
```
metric: decode_p95_ms
before (baseline): 24.6
after (canary): 56.3
increase: 2.29x
affected: shortseq traffic (<=64)
traces: high tail correlated with attention kernel switch to attentn_v2
```

perf-bot: alert created -> PERF-2026. Assigned to @arnav and @devon.

devon: quick profile (flamegraph) from a failing canary trace: outer decode loop spends 48% in kernel selector + 32% in attention kernel impl. KV cache ops show increased memcpy ops (~4x).

maya: hmm memcpy up 4x points to memcopy path being invoked more frequently — maybe the kernel choice changed memory layout assumptions. Did the PR change kv-cache alignment or buffer lifetimes?

arnav: I changed the heuristic that selects fused_attention vs split_attention based on observed microbatch shapes. No explicit mem layout change. The intention was to avoid small-mbatch kernel fallthrough.

lina: I pulled a trace and captured scheduler decisions for a shortseq request: selector picked attentn_v2 -> fused_op executor -> then evicted prefix-KV twice during decode (seen as two kv_evict calls). That eviction triggers memcpy on each re-alloc.

devon: interesting — so selector triggers a kernel that has higher KV working set causing eviction churn. Could be the new kernel uses a temp buffer strategy.

arnav: i can roll back the selector tweak in a canary to confirm. Which commit should we pin? revert candidate: d4f7b9c~1 (pre-heuristic).

zach: running quick bisect now across the last 6 merges spanning 6 hours. will update in ~15m.

sre-bot: deploy job #5941 started: canary group warmup.

(15m later)

zach: bisect update — narrowing to the scheduler heuristic commit in PR #3281. When pinned to the previous kernel preference, p95 returns to ~25ms.

maya: can we get a minimal repro? Shortseq request payload + config? I want to run local bench with exact microbatch sequence.

lina: repro stack: shortseq 1..32, batching policy: continuous 8ms, kv-cache enabled, suffix-attention=true. I saved a representative request and logs in /tmp/repro-4812.tgz on canary host.

arnav: thanks. I'll instrument more logs in selector to dump chosen kernels + their declared working set sizes. Adding counters for kv_eviction events.

devon: in parallel can we try forcing kernel preference to the older attentn_v1 for shortseq via runtime override? If that restores perf, we have a solid root cause.

zach: forced override applied on canary (runtime flag: --kernel-prefer=attn_v1 for seq<=64). After 5 warmup runs: p95=26.1ms. tail looks similar to baseline.

arnav: ok that's pretty conclusive. New heuristic is too eager to pick attn_v2 for certain short sequences which increases ephemeral memory and triggers KV eviction. I'll prepare a revert and a follow-up PR that adds a cache-awareness check (estimate working set + kv footprint).

maya: can we add an automated regression test in CI that simulates continuous batching + kv-cache with shortseq patterns? We should prevent this from regressing again.

devon: agreed. Add a micro-e2e perf test that asserts p95<35ms for that repro profile. Tagging as flaky-tolerant but will fail PRs on canary.

arnav: creating revert PR now (PR #3295). Will also add selector metrics and a canary-only flag to enable new heuristic for gradual rollout.

perf-bot: canary alert resolved after override. Closing temporary incident.

zach: note for postmortem: root cause = kernel preference heuristic ignoring KV cache working set; contributing factor = no perf-e2e test for shortseq+kv. Action items: revert, add cache-aware heuristic, add canary-only flag, add microperf test.

lina: also let's add a sticky fallback: if eviction count spikes during a single request, fallback to attn_v1 for rest of request to avoid repeated memcpy. Could be a quick mitigation.

arnav: good idea. I'll prototype fallback in the selector runtime path and keep it behind config.

devon: plan sounds solid. Please ping when PR #3295 is ready for review and when you have the perf test.

arnav: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3295 — revert + tests. Requesting quick review from @devon @maya.

maya: reviewing now.

(2h later)

maya: merged revert to canary. canary p95 returned to baseline across 3 nodes. we'll keep the new heuristic disabled by default until we add cache-awareness.

devon: thanks all. postmortem and follow-ups tracked in PERF-2026. Closing thread for now.
